purpose: Describe stable, observable material and spatial facts that a painter may render without inventing scene content.

gallery.title: The Gallery of Unfinished Things

facts: Frames and unfinished works occupy the walls at varied heights and intervals.
Faint rectangles, nail traces, and tonal ghosts remain where some works or frames previously hung.
Some works expose raw ground or underpainting instead of a finished image.
Some painted passages stop abruptly before reaching the edge of their support.
Some surfaces preserve erased, revised, or overwritten marks.
Completion is uneven: worked passages may sit beside raw or barely begun areas.
At least one beautifully made empty frame is a fixed part of the room.
Empty and unfinished framed works are not arranged as a perfectly symmetrical salon display.

traces: The walls preserve evidence that works have been moved, reconsidered, and rehung.
Unfinishedness is physically visible in surfaces and marks, not only inferred from absence.
spatialFacts: The room remains navigable toward the Hearth to the west and a quieter passage to the north.
Negative space between works is irregular rather than uniformly staged.
absences: No label explains what an unfinished work is supposed to become.
Not every frame contains a completed image.
